what_its_for: Tranylcypromine is an antidepressant used to treat depression, especially when other antidepressants have not worked. It belongs to a class of medicines called MAO inhibitors (MAOIs). It helps improve your mood, energy, sleep, and appetite by increasing certain natural chemicals in your brain.
how_to_take: Take tranylcypromine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. Do NOT crush or chew the tablet. This medicine requires very strict diet restrictions — you must avoid foods and drinks high in tyramine (see 'What to Avoid' section). Always carry your medication card or list with you to show any healthcare provider that you take an MAOI.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg twice a day (morning and afternoon). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time, usually up to 30 mg per day. Do not take a dose in the evening or at night because it can cause trouble sleeping. Never take more than your doctor prescribes. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first — your doctor will help you slowly reduce the dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still several hours before bedtime. If it is close to bedtime, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tranylcypromine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: DIET RESTRICTIONS ARE EXTREMELY IMPORTANT with this medicine. Eating high-tyramine foods while taking tranylcypromine can cause a sudden dangerous rise in blood pressure (hypertensive crisis). AVOID: aged cheeses (cheddar, brie, camembert, blue cheese), cured or fermented meats (salami, pepperoni, bologna, bacon), pickled or fermented foods (sauerkraut, kimchi, pickles), broad bean pods (fava beans), overripe or dried fruits, tap beer and red wine, soy sauce, miso, tofu, teriyaki sauce, and any spoiled or improperly stored foods. Also avoid: alcohol, caffeine in large amounts, and cold or allergy medicines, decongestants (like pseudoephedrine), pain relievers (like dextromethorphan in cough medicines), other antidepressants, stimulants, or herbal supplements (like St. John's Wort) unless your doctor approves. Always tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist that you take an MAOI before starting any new medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room immediately if you have: a sudden severe headache, stiff neck, fast or pounding heartbeat, chest pain, severe nausea or vomiting, sweating, or blurred vision — these could be signs of a dangerous rise in blood pressure (hypertensive crisis). Also call your doctor if you have: worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in mood or behavior, thoughts of harming yourself or others, restlessness or agitation, dizziness or fainting, fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or twitching (signs of serotonin syndrome), or any new or unusual symptoms. Seek emergency help if you think you may have taken too much of this medicine.
when_it_works: Tranylcypromine may start to improve your sleep and appetite within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, the full benefit for your mood and depression may take 3 to 6 weeks or longer. Do not stop taking it even if you do not feel better right away. Talk to your doctor before stopping.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution — you may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness or falls. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. The risks and benefits must be carefully considered. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Ask your doctor before breastfeeding. Children and teenagers: This medicine is not usually used in people under 18. Young adults up to age 24 should be closely monitored for changes in mood or thoughts of self-harm, especially in the first few weeks of treatment. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease — your dose may need to be adjusted.
